stemMd: An enzyme increases the rate at which a closed system approaches chemical equilibrium. Which quantity remains unchanged by the enzyme?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The rate of the forward reaction at a given nonequilibrium composition

options.label: B
options.textMd: The activation barrier for the catalysed pathway

options.label: C
options.textMd: The equilibrium constant of the reaction

options.label: D
options.textMd: The rate of the reverse reaction at a given nonequilibrium composition

options.label: E
options.textMd: The time needed to approach equilibrium

explanationMd: An enzyme changes kinetics, not the free-energy difference between reactants and products. It accelerates both directions through a lower-barrier pathway, allowing equilibrium to be reached sooner. The equilibrium constant is determined by thermodynamics and is unchanged at a fixed temperature.

distractorRationale.b: An enzyme provides a pathway with a lower activation barrier.
distractorRationale.d: The reverse process is catalysed as well.
